subject: Egress proof-of-possession + perimeter ACLs — kickoff & evidence request
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medicorp.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@medicorp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — request for evidence and allowlist

Chloe / Jordan,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. We need to complete the security team's checklist for our Private deployment (VPC, customer-managed NAT). Specifically the auditor needs: 

- Definitive list of outbound IPs that Redwood's control plane and private runtime will originate from (per-region if applicable)
- Firewall rules sample (ports, FQDNs, SNI) that we should allow from the VPC
- A short write-up describing your egress proof-of-possession process (how you confirm outbound IPs are under Redwood control vs. shared cloud ephemeral IPs)

Can you also include any pre-built evidence artifacts (e.g., signed IP ownership statements, public ASN references, or a ZIP with recent netflow/snippets) we can hand to our compliance team?

We're under a hard deadline for the vendor security review by May 7 — would you be able to get the artifacts to us by May 4?

Appreciate it,
Priya
Priya Singh
Security Program Manager — Medicorp

From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medicorp.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, NetOps Team <netops@medicorp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — request for evidence and allowlist

Thanks Priya — we can meet that timeline. Below is our plan and the artifacts we'll produce. We will deliver a single "egress evidence bundle" by Tue 2027-05-04.

Deliverables (what you'll receive):
- requested_ip_list.csv (per-region outbound IP CIDRs and representative NAT egress addresses)
- egres s-ports-and-urls.pdf (list of ports, recommended FQDN/SNI allowlist, and graceful fallback guidance)
- short POS (proof-of-possession) memo describing IP allocation and runbook steps we use to claim/rotate IPs
- optional: sample netflow snippets and an operations checklist for connection validation (egress-evidence-bundle.zip)

Technical notes for your NetOps team:
- Redwood Private uses dedicated NAT gateways for customer-controlled VPC deployments when requested; otherwise we offer customer-dedicated egress pools tied to reserved capacity. We will explicitly label which mode applies to Medicorp in the bundle.
- We will provide both the stable CIDR blocks and a small set of per-region ephemeral IPs used for bursts — the bundle will include guidance for whitelisting either the full CIDR or the stable addresses only.

Jordan will follow up with the exact firewall rule snippets and an annotated sample iptables/ACL for common vendor setups. Irene will include the compliance statement and evidence checklist. Markus will confirm rotation cadence and how we sign off on ownership.

Quick ask: Priya — can your team confirm whether Medicorp's firewall appliance accepts FQDN/SNI-based allowlists or if you need raw IPs only? That will change whether we prioritize CIDRs vs. per-host FQDN guidance.

—
Chloe Martin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medicorp.com>, chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@medicorp.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — request for evidence and allowlist

Priya — sample snippets below you can share with your NetOps lead. I've kept the examples intentionally conservative (allow CIDR / port ranges) and added notes for FQDN/SNI where helpful.

1) Minimal outbound ports we use (default):
- 443/tcp (primary TLS to control plane and artifact stores)
- 80/tcp (health checks / redirection only; not recommended as primary)
- 123/udp (NTP) — only if you require time sync to Redwood-managed endpoints

2) Example CIDR allowlist (representative; final CSV will include exact per-region blocks):
- 35.192.0.0/14  # control-plane-eu-west (example sample)
- 34.120.0.0/16  # control-plane-us-central
- 203.0.113.64/28 # reserved egress-pool-apac-burst

3) FQDN/SNI recommendations (preferred when firewall supports it):
- *.redwood-inference.net (control plane API endpoints)
- artifacts.redwood-inference.net (model store and artifact fetch)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.net (TLS endpoints for telemetry batching)

4) Example ACL snippet (Cisco ASA-ish pseudo):
object network RW_CONTROL_PLANE
 host 35.192.0.15
 nat (inside,outside) source static LOCAL_LOCAL LOCAL
access-list OUTBOUND extended permit tcp any object RW_CONTROL_PLANE eq 443

Notes and caveats:
- If you cannot do FQDN allowlist, whitelisting our stable CIDRs (first item in the CSV) is the recommended approach; ephemeral/burst IPs will be small and documented but may require a slightly broader CIDR if you prefer low-maintenance rules.
- We sign an IP-ownership statement and include ASN references where applicable. Those will appear in the POS memo.

I'll attach a quick PDF with these snippets and the port matrix.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medicorp.com>, chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, Matthew Lowe <m.lowe@secureaudits.io>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — request for evidence and allowlist

Priya / Medicorp audit team —

I've pulled together the compliance-oriented artifacts for the evidence bundle. Highlights: 

- POS memo (signed): describes IP assignment, where the IPs are advertised (cloud provider ranges + our registered ASN when applicable), and who is the owner inside Redwood.
- Recent netflow snippets (anonymized) showing egress sessions from a private runtime to control plane endpoints with timestamps.
- A checksum file listing the artifact filenames in the ZIP and a short validation script we use (verify-evidence.sh) to checksum the bundle.

Attachment: egres s-evidence-bundle.zip (contains POS memo, netflow-csvs, signed-ownership.txt, verify-evidence.sh)

We recommend your security reviewer validate the POS memo and run the verify script to ensure artifact integrity — that helps speed up attestation. If SecureAudits wants to see BGP/ASN delegation records, we can include the published routes and RIR records too; Matthew, do you want us to add those?

I will follow up with a short one-page compliance note mapping each artifact to the checklist items Medicorp shared.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Compliance Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medicorp.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@medicorp.com>, Matthew Lowe <m.lowe@secureaudits.io>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — request for evidence and allowlist

Team — many thanks, this is exactly what we needed. I've dropped the ZIP and the CSV into our internal ticket and forwarded it to the Medicorp firewall team. A couple quick answers to earlier questions: 

- Our appliance supports SNI/FQDN rules in the 7.x software release, so the FQDN guidance is preferred.
- We've downloaded the verify-evidence.sh and will run it as part of our intake.

Next steps from Medicorp side:
- NetOps will test connectivity to the sample IPs this week and will confirm by EOD Thu May 6.
- Security will review POS memo and, if anything else is needed, will loop in SecureAudits (Matthew).

I'll flag if any additional artifacts are requested. Thanks to everyone for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Priya
Priya Singh
Security Program Manager — Medicorp
